companies.name: Deel
companies.context: B2B SaaS HRIS and payroll company accused of orchestrating a corporate espionage operation against rival Rippling by recruiting a Rippling employee as a paid spy for 5,000 euros/month. CEO Alex Bouaziz and CFO/father Philippe Bouaziz allegedly coordinated payments using code words like 'send that watch to London.'

companies.name: Rippling
companies.context: B2B SaaS HRIS and payroll company that uncovered a Deel-recruited spy using a honeypot Slack channel and its own IT product, then filed a detailed 12-page affidavit. Hosts noted Rippling sales reps now have an exceptional opportunity to poach Deel clients.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.context: Delivered 336,000 vehicles in Q1 2025, a 13% decline year-over-year and below analyst expectations of 396,000; new registrations fell 76% in Germany in February and 11.6% in California. Shares rose 4% on release of the figures as markets had expected even worse results.

companies.name: Flexport
companies.context: Freight logistics platform whose CEO Ryan Petersen discussed tariff impacts, noting air freight from Chinese e-commerce is at major risk while customs advisory and domestic trucking businesses are booming. Petersen said Flexport estimates its market share at approximately 0.25%.

companies.name: Profound
companies.context: NYC-based marketing platform helping brands understand and improve visibility in LLM answer engines; raised a $3.5M seed round co-led by Keith Rabois and Coastal Adventures. Clients include MongoDB, Indeed, Mercury, Rippling, and Ramp, and the company helped Ramp increase LLM visibility by 7x.

companies.name: Bezel
companies.context: Watch marketplace platform whose co-founder Quaid Walker reported the company's best month ever while reporting live from Watches and Wonders in Geneva. Hosts noted it jokingly as the unofficial sponsor of the Deel spy watch-payment scheme.

companies.name: Roam
companies.context: Platform enabling homebuyers to assume sellers' existing low-rate FHA/VA mortgages; announced an $11.5M Series A led by Khosla Ventures and Founders Fund. Independent economists found sellers get 5% more and buyers save $700/month using the platform.

companies.name: Lightmatter
companies.context: MIT spinout building silicon photonic interconnects for AI data centers; announced 114 trillion bits per second bandwidth, roughly 100x the current state of the art of 1.6 trillion bits/second. The company's chips integrate with existing GPUs requiring no software changes.

companies.name: Vacheron Constantin
companies.context: Released the Solaria Ultra Grand Complication at Watches and Wonders featuring 41 complications and 1,521 components after 8 years of R&D and 13 patent applications. Hosts described the brand as being on a generational run.

companies.name: Rolex
companies.context: Debuted the Landweller at Watches and Wonders, its first new model in many years, featuring an integrated bracelet and new caliber 7135 escapement. Expected to sell well above its $14,000 retail price on the secondary market.

companies.name: Patek Philippe
companies.context: Released the 6196P Calatrava at Watches and Wonders, described as the best modern Calatrava in a long time featuring a salmon dial. Received a quieter reception than the Rolex Landweller.

companies.name: Audemars Piguet
companies.context: Did not formally participate in Watches and Wonders but quietly announced new Royal Oak ceramic color variants, including a new blue ceramic aligned with a specific Swiss valley sky color. The brand's absence from the event was noted as a deliberate choice.

companies.name: Ramp
companies.context: Corporate card and expense management platform; featured as both a sponsor and a Profound client that increased LLM visibility 7x. Ramp's applied AI team built and shipped an AI-generated receipt fraud detection feature in under 24 hours after ChatGPT's image model made fake receipt generation easy.

companies.name: Circle
companies.context: Stablecoin company that filed its S-1 for an IPO; crypto investor Omar at Dragonfly criticized the filing, arguing the ~$5B valuation is unjustified given distribution cost margin compression and imminent bank competition. Described as a possible Hail Mary for liquidity before banks crash the stablecoin market.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.context: ChatGPT's GPT-4o image model caused a viral Studio Ghibli moment demonstrating sequential token-based image generation with high controllability; discussed as planning to enter shoppability and agentic browsing within answer engines. Sam Altman referenced in context of a viral meme quote.

companies.name: Perplexity
companies.context: Cited as a leading answer engine replacing traditional blue-link search; Profound monitors brand visibility across Perplexity, ChatGPT, and Copilot. Described as a streaming-to-CDs type disruption moment for traditional search.

topics.name: Deel-Rippling Corporate Espionage Scandal
topics.summary: A Rippling employee was allegedly recruited by Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz in September 2024 to spy for 5,000 euros/month, passing client leads, talent intelligence, and internal strategies via Telegram. Payments were made via Revolut then Ethereum on blockchain.com by the COO's wife. The spy was caught via a honeypot Slack channel and a Tinybird keyword trap, then cooperated with Rippling after Deel's lawyer allegedly advised him to flee to Dubai. A 12-page affidavit details code words and implicates Deel's CEO, CFO/father, COO, and legal counsel.

topics.name: Tesla Q1 2025 Delivery Decline
topics.summary: Tesla delivered 336,000 vehicles in Q1 2025, down 13% year-over-year and well below analyst expectations of 396,000, with registrations falling 76% in Germany in February and 11.6% in California. Brand damage is linked to Elon Musk's DOGE role and political polarization, though shares rose 4% as the market had expected even worse results. Hosts discussed whether Elon could rebuild bipartisan brand appeal if he exits the administration.

topics.name: Liberation Day Tariffs
topics.summary: Trump announced reciprocal tariffs on April 2 including a 10% baseline on all imports, 34% on China, 20% on EU, 24% on Japan, and 31% on Switzerland. Ryan Petersen noted a cabinet secretary framed this as the start of negotiations rather than a final position. Markets responded with slight gains as the announcements roughly met expectations; Flexport's customs advisory business is booming from the uncertainty.

topics.name: Watches and Wonders 2025
topics.summary: Rolex debuted the Landweller, its first new model in many years, featuring an integrated bracelet and new caliber 7135 escapement, expected to sell at a major secondary market premium above its $14,000 retail price. Vacheron Constantin released the world's most complicated watch with 41 complications. The broader secondary watch market is recovering from its post-COVID correction with healthy demand on key references.

topics.name: AI Image Generation and the Studio Ghibli Moment
topics.summary: OpenAI's GPT-4o image model went viral generating Studio Ghibli-style images, using a sequential token-based architecture rather than diffusion, enabling higher controllability at the cost of more compute. Sarah Guo argued this proves image quality is far from solved and significant opportunity remains at the application layer for controllability, workflow, and vertical-specific tools.

topics.name: Answer Engine Optimization (AEO / GEO)
topics.summary: Profound's James Cadwallader described how brands face a zero-click future where AI answer engines steal the consumer relationship from brands; 40% of consumers already use AI search for shopping per an Adobe study. Key tactics include LLMs.txt files, structured data, verbose metadata, and creating content for retrieval agents rather than humans. Ramp increased LLM visibility 7x using Profound's platform.

topics.name: AI Hardware and Photonic Interconnects
topics.summary: Lightmatter's Nicholas Harris argued interconnect is now the primary AI scaling bottleneck, having improved only 1,000x over 30 years vs 1 million x for processors. The company announced 114 trillion bits/second photonic bandwidth (~100x state of the art) via silicon photonics 3D-stacked onto GPUs requiring zero software changes; commercial ramp expected in 2026-2027.

topics.name: Assumable Mortgages and Housing Affordability
topics.summary: Roam aggregated 1.5 trillion dollars worth of assumable FHA/VA mortgages originated at 2-3% rates, making them searchable and transactable for buyers seeking to escape today's 7% rate environment. Independent economists found sellers net 5% more and buyers save $700/month; Raunaq Singh described it as the only near-term solution to housing affordability ahead of any permit expansion taking effect.

topics.name: Global Trade and Tariff Impact on Logistics
topics.summary: Ryan Petersen noted effective duty rates on Chinese goods could reach 70-80% given stacked tariffs, but argued US dollar strength means tariffs alone will not reshore manufacturing. He advocated for gradual, pre-announced tariff schedules to allow supply chain planning; Flexport's customs advisory business is booming while its air freight from China faces major headwinds.

topics.name: Circle IPO Filing
topics.summary: Circle filed its S-1 for an IPO with a rumored ~$5B valuation; Dragonfly's Omar posted a critical take noting distribution costs paid to Coinbase are crushing margins, core interest rate income is declining, and banks are about to launch competing stablecoins. The filing was described by one host as potentially a Hail Mary for founder liquidity before the competitive landscape tightens.

topics.name: Humanoid Robots and Automation
topics.summary: Discussion ranged from Unitree's $3,000 consumer robots on Amazon to Tesla's Optimus, with Elon claiming FSD and Optimus could justify a $30 trillion Tesla market cap. Consensus was that the technology is real and commercially available in early form but mass-scale deployment remains years away; Chinese manufacturers are leading on hardware shipping.

topics.name: Space-Based Solar Energy
topics.summary: Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt's new company Aetherflux plans to collect solar energy in orbit and beam it to Earth via lasers, with Chad Byers announcing a small angel investment. Hosts noted the economics depend heavily on launch cost trajectories and that the concept raises questions about space junk and visual sky impact.

topics.name: Future Freight Modalities
topics.summary: Autonomous trucking discussed as enabling 24/7 cross-country transit vs. the current 8-hour driver limit, with truck driving as the top profession in 34 US states. Ryan Petersen also expressed cautious excitement about airships (same volume as a 747, three-day ocean crossing at a price between air and ocean freight) and Zipline's sub-5-minute drone delivery in Dallas.

topics.name: AI Startup Strategy and Investment Thesis
topics.summary: Sarah Guo advised founders to watch what the labs are building and avoid flying too close to the sun on capabilities OpenAI and Anthropic clearly intend to own. She emphasized revenue durability vs 'chicken nugget revenue,' highlighted TAM expansion in legal (Harvey) and healthcare as genuinely exciting, and warned against assuming private equity financial expertise is easy to replicate.

topics.name: TikTok Acquisition
topics.summary: AppLovin and Amazon were noted as emerging bidders for TikTok ahead of a deadline, joining previously listed candidates on Polymarket including Perplexity, Larry Ellison, and Oracle. Hosts noted AppLovin has the market cap and ad-tech synergies to be a credible buyer.
